budget: one run per approved target. A re-run is allowed only for a bug fix written under 'amendments' before the re-run; the first run's numbers are kept and reported as superseded.
banned_moves_note: Adds rows by a rule fixed before any score; excludes no material after seeing its influence (R30_PF's absence from CR follows the existing CR entry filter and the complete-layer rule below, both fixed now). The pHRR material pool grows (65 -> 70), never shrinks. No thermal-property join: log_kpc stays the product's own FSRI HFM value exactly as exp043/exp074 already use it, and HFM is never layer-mapped. STA N2 residue stays a feature, never the target. The win rule is not touched: there are no candidates, and the snapshot rule is declared before any score. No hand edits of leaderboard/xlsx/numbers_of_record.
what: Five FSRI composite products have cone data but no MCC or STA of their own, because FSRI ran MCC/STA on their layers. Today they drop out of the pHRR set (has_mcc inner join) and the CR set (STA at any rate AND MCC char yield). This config gives each product MCC and STA features computed from its layers by one fixed rule, merges the overstuffed chair assembly and its three layers into one CV group, and re-scores the number-of-record config unchanged on the enlarged snapshot. That snapshot then becomes the benchmark of record for the approved target(s), whichever way the number moves.

rule.aggregation: UNWEIGHTED MEAN OVER THE LAYERS WITH DATA, two stages. Stage 1 (unchanged): each layer gets the existing per-material aggregate exactly as the record pipeline computes it for any material, i.e. the mean over that material's replicate rows (per heating rate for STA; pandas mean, skipna). Stage 2 (new): for each product p and each feature column, value(p) = arithmetic mean of the stage-1 values of p's layers that are non-NaN in that column, each layer weighted 1 regardless of its replicate count; NaN if no layer has a value. Implementation: agg.reindex(layers[p]).mean(axis=0, skipna=True). Values are used as stored: no clipping, zeroing or rounding (e.g. the gypsum core's -0.038 kJ/g total HR enters as is).

mapped_columns.pHRR (T.load internals): mcc_agg: mcc_peak_hrr_Wg, mcc_peak_norm_Wg, mcc_char_yield_pct (mcc_hrr.csv); x_agg: mcc_total_hr_kJg (= total_hr_bc_kJg), mcc_t_peak_C, mcc_t_onset_C (= t_onset_bc_C) (mcc_extras_fsri.csv)
mapped_columns.CR (data_cr internals): sta_wide: sta_res_3K, sta_res_10K, sta_res_30K (char_yield_sta.csv final_residual_mass_pct); mcc_agg: mcc_char_yield_pct, mcc_peak_hrr_Wg (mcc_hrr.csv)

rule.not_mapped: Everything else comes from the product's own rows, exactly as for any other material: heat flux and labels from the product's cone rows; density_kgm3, cone_thickness_mm, cone_mass_per_area_kgm2, categories and the category column from the product's material_props_fsri.csv row; log_kpc from the product's own HFM (Dry, lowest setpoint, T.ambient_dry). The plan maps MCC and STA only, and mapping HFM would bring in no extra value anyway (the only layers with HFM, the chair layers, are Wet-only, so their log_kpc is NaN).
rule.table_insertion: map_layers(agg) is applied to each per-material aggregate table (indexed by material) before the record pipeline's merges. It appends one row per product. A product row is appended only if at least one of its layers has a non-NaN value somewhere in that table; otherwise the product stays absent from that table, as it is today (this is why R30_PF gets no sta_wide row). Assert that no product is already in any table before insertion.
rule.complete_layer_entry_rule: A composite enters a target only if EVERY one of its layers has that target's entry-defining features at stage 1. pHRR: mcc_peak_hrr_Wg and mcc_char_yield_pct (T.BASE minus heat flux). CR: STA at one or more heating rates AND mcc_char_yield_pct. On the in-hand data this changes nothing beyond the existing filters: all 5 products pass for pHRR; 4 pass for CR and R30_PF fails, because neither layer has STA. The builder asserts that row sets with and without this rule are identical. It is declared so that a future partial-coverage composite cannot enter on one layer's value.
why_exposed_face_is_rejected (physics, f: Both targets are whole-specimen measurements. CR is final/initial specimen mass. pHRR is heat release per exposed area from a specimen whose substrate keeps burning or shielding once the face is gone. The exposed face is a thin, low-mass layer in every product: gypsum-board paper, the laminate sheet over 39.6 mm of particle board, the kraft facing on 50 mm of fiberglass, and the 0.47 mm chair fabric (about 0.19 of 1.61 kg/m2).

An exposed-face rule would give both gypsum boards the paper's MCC and STA (char yield about 17%, peak about 75 W/g). That says the product is paper, when it is mostly gypsum. For CR this is wrong for every inert-core product, and for pHRR it ignores the substrate that controls burning after the face is consumed.

It is also not defined from the data: material.json does not say which face was exposed in the cone for R30_PF, and the plan's other options (min, max, 'dominant layer') each need a per-product or per-feature judgement.

The unweighted mean is also physically wrong for gypsum: the mapped features are 48-50% residue for a mostly-gypsum product (prior_looks). It is chosen as the only rule that needs no per-product judgement, not because it is right. The plan expects C1 to lower the scores.
rule.also_rejected_ex_ante (never computed, n: exposed-face; min or max over layers; core-only / dominant layer; feature-specific rules (e.g. min for onset temperatures); mass-weighted means (no mass fractions exist for 4 of the 5 products; for the chair see open_questions); pooling layer replicates before averaging (it would weight layers by replicate count).

mapped_values (label-free, computed whil.note: Gypsum_Wallboard mcc_t_onset_C is the paper layer alone, because the core's onset is NaN ('layers with data'). mcc_peak_norm_Wg equals mcc_peak_hrr_Wg for every product (all layers at 0.5 C/s); it is mapped but is not a feature of either record model.

groups.rule: group = material, then PlasticC -> HIPS (existing merge), then {Overstuffed_Chair_Assembly, Overstuffed_Chair_Polyurethane_Foam, Overstuffed_Chair_Polyester_Batting, Overstuffed_Chair_Polyester_Fabric} -> 'Overstuffed_Chair_Assembly'. In general, a composite shares one group with every layer that has cone rows of its own; only the chair qualifies.
groups.why: The assembly's features are now built from its layers' MCC/STA, and each layer has its own cone rows (9 each in pHRR replicates; 9 / 7 / 9 CR rows). As separate groups, the model could train on a layer's features and label while testing the assembly, and the reverse. Merging is the same treatment as PlasticC -> HIPS. The other four products' layers have no cone rows, so they are never tested and need no link.
groups.not_linked (declared): Different FSRI products of similar make-up stay separate groups, as in exp074/exp117 and cr_round2.json: Particleboard (standalone sheet, 583 kg/m3) vs the countertop's particle-board layer; Fiberglass_Insulation_R30 and Fiberglass_Insulation_R13_Paper_Faced vs R30_PF (neither is in either C1 population); PMMA vs Black_PMMA, XPS vs EPS_Foam_Board and similar pairs (unchanged).

procedure (per approved target, in this.S1_merge_only (report-only): the incumbent config on the OLD rows (191 / 567, old features) with the C1 groups (pHRR 62 groups, CR 59). This isolates the chair-merge effect from the new rows. Never a record.
procedure (per approved target, in this.S2_snapshot (the record): the incumbent config on the C1 snapshot (205 rows / 66 groups; 603 rows / 62 groups): eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold(model, X, y, groups, n_splits=5, repeats=10, log_target=True for pHRR / False for CR), i.e. GroupKFold(shuffle=True, random_state=r) for r = 0..9; repeat-0 bootstrap_ci(y, oof[0], groups) with n_boot 2000, seed 0. snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.rule: For each approved target, the C1 snapshot becomes the benchmark population of record, and S2's rkf_mean and repeat-0 CI become the number of record after the critic, WHICHEVER WAY IT MOVES relative to the current record (exp074 0.6113 / exp117 0.6504 or round 9's successor). This mirrors loi_snapshot_update2.json: the bigger snapshot is the benchmark whichever way the number moves.
snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.no_adoption_gate: There are no candidates, so there is no selection, no 8/10 paired rule, and adoption_gate_v2.json does not apply (its scope.does_not_apply_to lists C1's re-baseline).
snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.independence: No later choice (model, feature, row, group or rule) may depend on the S2 score. A lower S2 is reported as a population change, never as a model regression; a higher S2 is never described as a model improvement or as progress toward the bar.
snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.critic: Critic pass in a fresh context before numbers_of_record.json changes. The critic may block for a bug (amendment plus one re-run). It may not reject the snapshot because the number fell, and may not propose a different layer rule, group rule or row set.
snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.record_text: The orchestrator's numbers_of_record note must say: 'C1 snapshot (FSRI composite layer mapping, experiments/configs/fsri_composite_snapshot.json): <n> rows / <m> materials / <g> groups; unweighted layer-mean MCC/STA for 5 (pHRR) or 4 (CR) composite products; chair assembly + 3 layers one group; previous record <exp> <value> [<lo>, <hi>] on <old rows>'. pHRR keeps 'comparable: pending-human' and the H5 wording ('ahead of the published number ... different population') only if S2 ci_lo > 0.30; see exit_triggers.
snapshot_rule (LOI-style, fixed before a.per_target: D5 may approve pHRR, CR or both. An unapproved target keeps its current population and record; nothing is computed for it.

outputs.result_jsons: experiments/results/fsri_composite_snapshot_phrr.json and fsri_composite_snapshot_cr.json (S2 only), in the existing schema: slug, target, round_config 'experiments/configs/fsri_composite_snapshot.json', dataset (snapshot description with rows/materials/groups), features, model, hyperparameters ('<record exp> config; unchanged'), code, n_rows, n_groups, protocol ('rgkf5x10' for pHRR, 'gkf_group5x10' for CR, as their records), rkf_mean, rkf_std, ci_lo, ci_hi (rounded to 4), paired_vs '', paired_delta 0.0, paired_wins 'n/a (snapshot re-score)', sota 0.30 / 0.82, sota_source 'pomazi_2026', status ('ok', or 'blocked' with blocked_reason set when a BLOCKED trigger fires), blocked_reason, note; plus pooled_ci_lo/hi, gss_mean (pHRR), category_grouped_mean/ci_lo/ci_hi, full-precision rkf_mean_full, ci_lo_full, ci_hi_full, per_repeat_r2 (10 floats), n_materials, snapshot 'C1'. The leaderboard exp ID is assigned by the orchestrator / scripts/update_trackers.py as usual.
outputs.diagnostics: experiments/runs/fsri_composite_snapshot_<phrr|cr>_diag.json: S0 reproduction values, S1 values, and the reported_only items below.
outputs.oof: experiments/runs/fsri_composite_snapshot_<phrr|cr>_oof.npz: y, groups, material, heat_flux, is_new (bool), row_id (snapshot order), category (n, the category-GKF groups after the chair rule), oof_S2 (10 x n), oof_catS2 (10 x n, category-GKF), oof_S1 (10 x n_old), oof_S0 (10 x n_old). Under 1 MB each; committed with the results so the critic can recompute every OOF-based diagnostic (the GroupShuffleSplit mean is re-run, not recomputed).

reported_only (computed for S2 of each a.standard: rkf mean/std, per-repeat R2, repeat-0 bootstrap CI, pooled-repeat CI = bootstrap_ci(y, oof.mean(axis=0), groups); pHRR also GroupShuffleSplit x10 mean (grouped_shuffle_r2 with the C1 groups, log_target=True), for continuity with exp074.
reported_only (computed for S2 of each a.category_gkf: repeated_group_kfold with groups = category, r = 0..9; CI = bootstrap_ci(y, coof[0], C1 groups). pHRR category = T.load's 'category' (first listed category, stripped, 'uncategorized' if missing). CR category = first listed category, stripped, lower-cased, 'none' if missing (as cr_round2.json). Chair rule: all 4 chair-group materials take the assembly's first category 'upholstered furniture' (batting and foam would otherwise be 'general polymer'), so the merged group is never split across category folds. 11 categories on both snapshots. Continuity: pHRR exp074 category-GKF 0.392 [-0.149, 0.529].
reported_only (computed for S2 of each a.decomposition: S0 (record, old rows, old groups), S1 (old rows, C1 groups) and S2 (record on C1 snapshot) rkf means and repeat-0 CIs side by side; each CI = bootstrap_ci(y, oof[0], that run's own groups), n_boot 2000, seed 0 (for S1: the C1 groups restricted to the old rows). Plus, from S2's OOF: mean over r = 0..9 of r2_score(y[s], oof_S2[r, s]) for s = old rows only (191 / 567) and s = new rows only (14 / 36), each against that subset's own mean; and the new rows' SSE share = sum over the new rows and the 10 repeats of (y - oof_S2[r])^2, divided by the same sum over all snapshot rows. Labelled 'not paired; folds differ'.
reported_only (computed for S2 of each a.per_composite_table: for each composite product in the target and each chair layer: n rows, mean y, mean OOF prediction (over its rows and the 10 S2 repeats), mean absolute error (mean over its rows and the 10 repeats of |y - oof_S2[r]|), and SSE share (sum over its rows and the 10 repeats of (y - oof_S2[r])^2, divided by the same sum over all snapshot rows). Diagnostic only; acting on it (excluding or reweighting a product) is banned.
reported_only (computed for S2 of each a.pHRR_truncation_note: number of composite replicates behind the new pHRR rows that carry truncated_test (25 of 42 in the current table: R30_PF 9, Gypsum_Wallboard 6, Lightweight_Gypsum_Wallboard 9, chair assembly 1). They are kept by the existing pHRR target definition; reported, never acted on.

never_reported: Any score under another layer rule (exposed face, min, max, core-only, mass-weighted, feature-specific); S2 with the chair unmerged; S2 minus any composite or minus any material (except the pre-declared old-row / new-row subset diagnostics); any candidate model on the C1 snapshot inside this config; any other seed, fold seed or n_boot.
exit_triggers: CR: S2 ci_lo > 0.82 -> EXIT (claim question for humans; never write 'beats SOTA'; comparable stays 'pending-human'). pHRR: S2 ci_lo <= 0.30 -> EXIT with a blocker. The CI-clear status and H5 wording no longer hold, which changes how a number of record is described. The number still becomes the record by the snapshot rule after the critic, but the status wording is Arnav's call. pHRR S2 ci_lo > 0.30 is the existing state, not a new trigger. BLOCKED (blocker file, no record change): step-1 or self-test failure, any assertion failure, non-finite OOF, version or clone mismatch, an uncovered record config (incumbent_at_run_time), or another pHRR/CR round in flight (precondition_order).
expected_effect (deliberately unscored;: -0.05 to +0.02 per target; expect it to hurt. The point is breadth: two near-inert gypsum boards, a countertop, a faced batt and the chair assembly, in the residue range that drives CR variance. pHRR stays 'ahead, different population' unless ci_lo falls to 0.30 or below; CR stays below 0.82.
honesty_notes: This is a population change. S2 numbers are not comparable to exp074 / exp117 and must never be quoted as a delta against them without the words 'different population'.

The unweighted layer mean is a declared form, not physics. For gypsum it gives 48-50% residue features for a mostly-gypsum product whose cone residue is about 92-95% (a label look; see prior_looks). The gypsum boards are expected to be badly predicted on CR.
The exposed-face rule was rejected on physics before any score. The reasoning used the known fact that gypsum boards leave about 92% residue, so the rejection is not label-blind; see prior_looks.
Gypsum_Wallboard contributes only 2 pHRR rows (one group); its 25 kW/m2 replicates did not ignite.
The chair merge also changes the folds for old rows; S1 shows that effect alone.
The snapshot also moves the fold assignment of every other material, so part of any S0 -> S2 change is fold reshuffling, not the new rows (LOI snapshot 3 lost about half its drop to this).
Most new pHRR cells come from replicates flagged truncated_test; the existing target definition keeps them.
